properties.name: A server started with --read-only where there is no design store serves the latent surface and creates nothing (stdio, --http, --serve-shared), and "may this open create a store?" is one rule
properties.rationale: THE CAUSE, confirmed on main 293f957 by measurement (measure-main.log) and by tests observed failing there: every serving path in main() opened --graph-path with ReflowService::new_reporting, which creates a missing store, BEFORE into_read_only was applied; the store-existence test that would have stopped it had three copies (one_shot step 4, the --shared client, LatentService::promoted) and the serving modes had none. The class is a guard written for one mode protecting only that mode — the same shape item 1 found in main()'s early returns — so the fix is one rule asked by every mode, held by a scan test, not a fourth copy. Anthony chose the surface (dec:a-read-only-server-with-no-store-serves-the-latent-surface). TWO DEFECTS FOUND ON THE WAY AND FIXED, because serving the latent surface over HTTP needed the same door: --only-if-present --http served the latent surface on STDIO (a server with stdin closed exited and nothing listened), and a design the latent surface opened went without the operator's --export-to (and over HTTP would have gone without the caller rule, the GitHub #616 fix-4 class). LEFT OUT, deliberately: a --shared CLIENT with --read-only and no store keeps item 1b's answer (the degraded surface naming --read-only, no daemon spawned) — a latent surface there would open a later store in-process and hold the lock against the shared daemon; a --serve-shared latent server that later serves a design does not publish a rendezvous then either; the registry needed no change beyond asking the rule (it binds only a store discovery found, re-read per request), and a sub-millisecond race between that read and the open remains. BOUND OF THE CLAIM: nothing is created while there is no store; once a store exists, opening it read-only still does RocksDB's housekeeping and refreshes the records beside it, as item 1 measured.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Every serving mode (stdio, --http, --serve-shared) started with --read-only where opening the path would create the store now serves the LATENT surface instead, on the transport it was given, and creates nothing: no store, no stamp, nothing beside it; --serve-shared publishes no rendezvous (SharedServer::publishes) but keeps its idle stop. The handshake says there is no design store and that --read-only creates none; reflow2_start_design is refused; describe_designs answers; over HTTP /readyz says 503 (readiness::NO_DESIGN_HERE) until a design is served. A store that appears later is opened read-only by the next call and served with no restart. The latent surface was made fit for HTTP: each session gets its own share of a promoted design, a session connecting after promotion is the design's from its handshake, the open runs off the runtime threads, a stop closes what it opened (drain::Holds::Latent), and a design it opens is readied by the server's own preparation (ServeAs: read-only, tree root, --export-to, caller rule). "May this open create a store?" is one function (opening.rs), now asked by one_shot::resolve_design, the --shared client, LatentService and registry discovery as well as the new serving check; a unit test scans src/ for any other copy. --read-only --help no longer names an exception. MERGE TRAIN (#662, #663, #665, #666, 2026-10-03): main had since gained describe_tools (#667, --describe and --list-tools), which tested Path::new(&cli.graph_path).exists() itself, a fifth copy the scan test caught; it asks opening::store_exists now.
